slot.brief: A source moving at constant speed towards then away from a stationary observer; ask for the ratio of the apparent frequencies in the two cases, or include wind/medium effects at high rigour.

stem: A source emitting frequency $f_0$ moves at $120$ m s$^{-1}$ along a straight track past a stationary observer. A uniform wind blows along the track in the source’s direction at $60$ m s$^{-1}$; sound speed relative to air is $300$ m s$^{-1}$. What is the ratio of the observed frequency while approaching to that while receding?

verdicts.working: In the source’s direction, sound travels at 360 m/s relative to the ground; against the wind, it travels at 240 m/s. Thus f_approach = 360/(360−120) f₀ = 3f₀/2, and f_recede = 240/(240+120) f₀ = 2f₀/3. Their ratio is 9/4.

working:
$f_{\rm app}=f_0\dfrac{c+w}{c+w-v}=f_0\dfrac{360}{240}=\dfrac32f_0$; $f_{\rm rec}=f_0\dfrac{c-w}{c-w+v}=f_0\dfrac{240}{360}=\dfrac23f_0$; $\dfrac{f_{\rm app}}{f_{\rm rec}}=\dfrac94$.

Independent check: In the source’s direction, sound travels at 360 m/s relative to the ground; against the wind, it travels at 240 m/s. Thus f_approach = 360/(360−120) f₀ = 3f₀/2, and f_recede = 240/(240+120) f₀ = 2f₀/3. Their ratio is 9/4.
solution:
With wind speed $w$ along the source’s motion, the sound speeds along and against the wind are $c+w=360$ and $c-w=240$ m s$^{-1}$.
$$\frac{f_{\rm app}}{f_{\rm rec}}=\frac{(c+w)/(c+w-v)}{(c-w)/(c-w+v)}=\frac{360/240}{240/360}=\frac94$$
